P1.evidence: No setter notes read back — the rep admitted he had not seen the application: 'I didn't see it come by, so please refresh me' and 'see anything come true like in a film form or anything.' The frame was three-part not four: 'go through where you're currently at, where you want to go. See if we can help you bridge that gap.' Frame agreement was taken ('Okay?' / 'Okay. Great.'). The opening question was 'take me through, yeah, sort of where you're currently at at the moment when it comes to fitness' — a where-are-you question rather than the scripted 'what are you potentially looking for help with?'

P2.evidence: Age asked and answered ('How old are you currently?' / 'I'll be 48 next month'), but height and weight were never asked; body fat was volunteered, not requested. Occupation was only asked at 01:09:00 — over an hour in and well after the offer — and with no desk-bound-vs-on-feet follow-up. Health was probed only via joints and mobility, never conditions or hereditary risk. Injuries were properly worked: 'when it comes to your joints at the moment, like how are they?' plus a good probe for hips, back and hamstrings. Training week and diet both covered in detail. Results from current training, sleep and energy were never asked at all.

P3.evidence: The strongest phase. The bridge was run cleanly: 'that's all fitness-wise. But then outside of the fitness, why is this important for you to do this at 47?' He drove the future-pace ('10 years from now, you're still moving in the way that you want to move. How would that be for you?'), pushed to impact on others ('how do you think that that would be for you also when you show that to your daughters that you're actually leading by example'), and reached family and legacy. The reflect-back was softer than scripted — 'from what I'm hearing, it's more of a, you want to make sure you're doing the right thing because you're older' — and he never asked for one physical thing the prospect currently cannot do.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were only mapped as a training history the prospect volunteered (magazines, calisthenics, four years back in the gym); the rep never asked what happened with them or why they did not stick. The closest to the root-cause move was 'why do you think that you aren't just going to take the same approach, just figure it out over a long period of time, just by reading some papers, by watching some videos?' — which probes why-a-coach rather than why-it-failed. No gap was ever named by the prospect, and the structure-not-effort frame was never landed. This is the phase that would have surfaced the financial constraint before the price was presented.

P5.evidence: Full consequence frame run: 'let's say you continue doing the workouts that you're doing at the moment... 10 years from now you're 57 and yeah all of that has slowly been getting worse over time... like how would that be for you?' followed by the settle question verbatim — 'Are you willing to settle for a life where that is not the case, where your biological age isn't less?' Prospect: 'No. I don't want to settle for that.' The rep did not ask 'why not?' — the prospect offered the reason unprompted. The line in the sand was replaced with an effort commitment: 'are you then also actually going to put in the effort that you need to put in to get to the outcome?'

P6.evidence: Belief check ran after the presentation rather than before it: 'do you feel like you're actually going to be able to get to those goals of 12% body fat, more checked, when your mobility gets better?' — answered yes. The all-in check ('if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in') was never asked, which is exactly the question that would have surfaced the budget constraint before the $6,000 landed. The rep did get a yes before presenting the investment ('So are you ready to also get that started?' / 'Yes'), but it was a thin yes and hesitation later surfaced repeatedly without a return to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted but never landed — the prospect deferred ('I think I should let it go for another few months') and the rep conceded. No payment, no Trevor onboarding call, no agreement email, no Skool link. The phase was unreachable rather than skipped.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran ('just a triple check, right? Like outside of the money aspect, do you feel like, Richard, I do want to get started with this'). The should-vs-how reframe never appeared in words but was implied. The break-it-up move ran ('we can have a chat about it, see if we can actually make something work'). Of the financial picture, only two of six items were collected: cash on hand ('what do you currently have set aside... that you can actually put towards something like this' → $2,000) and monthly surplus ('what do you usually have left over after that' → ~$1,000). Credit cards, available credit, used-vs-available and investments were never asked. He also never asked permission for the open financial conversation before starting it.

Triggered twice — 'See I have to think about it' at 00:49:00 and 'Let me think about this' at 00:56:29. The rep ran the surface-the-blocker move well ('Before you go and think about it... What's like the main thing that's coming up?'). None of the deciding moves ran: no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', no 'that man you want to be — how does HE decide right now?'. Instead he re-presented the discounted trial month, which converts an OA into a price concession.

Trigger was family rather than spouse specifically ('it's the kind of decision I have to take with now', 'it's the kind of decisions that I have to change with my family'). Ran: what obstacles come up when you talk to them ('what do you think that they would say on the first sense?'), the permission-vs-responsibility reframe ('it sounds like you're putting the responsibility a little bit on them of giving you the permission of doing it'), and whose responsibility the work is. Did not run 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', and did not offer the scripted deposit-with-full-refund fallback. He did add an unscripted move — predicting the family would talk him out of it — which is closer to pressure than to the play.

Trigger landed at the end: 'I think I should let it go for another few months' and 'it's better to show up in some months from here.' The rep ran one move — 'Why would you put it on the back burner then for another few months? That's what I'm trying to understand' — and then conceded. None of the core OD moves ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets — metabolism slows, injuries compound', no 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled'. Given the prospect's stated longevity anxiety this was the strongest available play and it was left on the table.

The rep introduced the trigger himself ('could it be that you have a little bit of uncertainty for yourself to actually make the decision?') and the prospect confirmed with a specific fear — 'I've got myself into financial problems with all decisions... I don't want to make the mistakes I did in the past.' The rep ran the burned-before probe ('are they sort of in a similar realm?') then abandoned it in favour of asserting 'this is zero risk', which is a claim rather than a play and is not supported by the terms he had just described. The certainty question, the pleasure/pain question and the plane metaphor for fear were not used; the plane appeared instead as an oxygen-mask analogy inside the family objection.

Script gap: the prospect's blocker was not capacity or willingness in the abstract but an already-allocated household budget — money earmarked for his eldest daughter's car and college costs. The playbook has no move for competing committed capital, so the rep improvised by putting the prospect's health against his daughter's car ('do you think that she would rather just have a car?'). That is the highest-risk improvisation in the call and there is no scripted alternative for it.

notes: P3 and P5 were genuinely well run — the why was reached, the consequence frame landed, and the prospect said out loud he would not settle. The call was then lost in P4 and P6: past attempts and root cause were never worked, and the all-in commitment check was skipped, so a household budget constraint that was always going to decide this call only surfaced after the price. Coaching priority is to run P6b before presenting, and to stop discounting into a think-about-it: the price moved $6,000 → three-way split → a $1,200 'trial month' inside four minutes on hesitation alone, and none of that recovered the deal.
